name: Prefab Building Construction
description:
Prefab Building Construction — Design, Fabricate, Erect

Prefab building construction with SAMAN means we design, fabricate, and erect a complete building for you — not just supply panels and leave the assembly to someone else. We manufacture at our own facilities in Bangalore and Greater Noida and construct prefabricated commercial and industrial buildings across India. The build shown on this page is an 80 × 30 × 20 ft structure — 2,400 sq ft of floor area with a 20 ft eave height — built on a structural steel frame with PUF sandwich panels, constructed and handed over for ₹23,65,000 to ₹23,75,000, inclusive of all taxes.

How Is a Prefab Building Constructed?

Site erection in progress — factory-fabricated portal frames bolted together by the crew before cladding.

A prefab building is constructed in a defined sequence: a site survey and structural design come first; structural components and wall panels are then factory-fabricated to that design, transported to site, and assembled by an erection crew; finishing and a handover inspection close the project. The factory build and your civil foundation run in parallel, which is where the time saving comes from.

Because the structural steel frame and the panels are made as factory-fabricated components, the on-site phase is assembly rather than wet construction. Your foundation can be poured to our layout drawing while fabrication is still running at our plant, so the two timelines overlap instead of stacking. That parallel sequence is the core difference between prefabricated building construction and a conventional brick-and-RCC build.

Three Construction Formats — and When Each One Fits

Not every prefab building is built the same way. The right format depends on your span, your intended use, and whether you may relocate the building later.

The steel-frame format — wide clear spans suited to workshops and warehouses.

Construction format Best suited for Typical clear span Relocatable
Panel-built (sandwich panel on light frame) Offices, site buildings, lighter commercial use Up to ~9 m Partly — panels demount
Modular volumetric (rooms craned in) Multi-room offices needing fast occupancy Up to ~7 m per module Yes — whole modules
Steel-frame (PEB-grade portal frame) Workshops, warehouses, wide-span industrial 9–30 m and above No — permanent

For lighter offices and site accommodation, panel-built is the quickest and most cost-efficient. Where you need a wide, column-free interior — a workshop or warehouse — prefab metal building construction on a PEB-grade portal frame is the right call, and the 80 × 30 × 20 ft build on this page uses exactly that steel-frame method with PUF panel cladding.

What SAMAN Builds and Hands Over — the 80 × 30 × 20 ft Build

The 80 × 30 × 20 ft build — white PUF sandwich panels, charcoal trim, constructed and handed over.

This configuration is a 2,400 sq ft building on a structural steel frame, clad in PUF sandwich panels, delivered at ₹23,65,000–₹23,75,000 inclusive of taxes. Our construction scope covers the steel frame, wall and roof panels, doors and windows as configured, transport, site assembly by our own erection crew, and handover. You arrange two things: a level plinth or foundation poured to the layout drawing we issue, and utility connections after structural handover. For the full single-contract scope on larger projects — including IS-code documentation and civil coordination — see our turnkey PEB construction service.

Choosing Your Prefab Building Construction Path

A handed-over prefab building in daily commercial use on an industrial compound.

This page covers the building constructed and handed over as a service at a fixed configuration; other sizes follow the same construction service, quoted per square foot. If instead you want to specify and buy the building as a finished product, our range of prefab buildings is the better starting point. If you already have an erection team and need only the fabricated steel structure delivered to site, source it as pre-engineered building structures instead. And if your requirement is a simpler single-span shed rather than a finished building, our industrial sheds are built to that purpose.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does prefab building construction take compared with conventional construction?

For a building of this scale, the constructed-and-handed-over timeline runs roughly 30 to 45 days from order, against 6 to 10 months for an equivalent conventional RCC build. The saving comes from running factory fabrication and your site foundation in parallel rather than in sequence.

What does it cost to construct a prefab building of this size?

The 80 × 30 × 20 ft (2,400 sq ft) steel-frame build on this page is ₹23,65,000–₹23,75,000 inclusive of taxes — about ₹985 per sq ft for the constructed structure. Larger or differently configured buildings are quoted per square foot on the same construction service.

Is this a construction service, or am I buying a finished building?

This is a construction service: we design, fabricate, and erect the building on your site and hand it over. If you would rather select and purchase a building as a ready product line, that is handled on our prefab buildings pages instead.

Can a prefab building be expanded or relocated after it is constructed?

It depends on the format. Modular volumetric and panel-built structures can be partly demounted and relocated; a steel-frame building like this one is designed as a permanent structure, though it can be planned at design stage to accept future bays.

A multi-bay prefab building complex — the scale SAMAN constructs under one project.

Prefabricated construction is a building method in which the structural components — frames, wall and roof panels, and sometimes whole modules — are manufactured in a factory and then transported to your site for assembly, and at SAMAN we design, build, and hand over commercial and industrial buildings this way from our facilities in Bangalore and Greater Noida. It replaces most of the wet, weather-exposed work of a conventional build with controlled factory production and a short on-site assembly phase.

Prefabricated construction on an industrial plot — factory-made components assembled into a finished building.

What prefabricated construction means

Prefabricated construction means a building's parts are made off-site in a factory under controlled conditions, then delivered and bolted together on a prepared foundation. Instead of casting and laying everything on site, the structure arrives as finished components — steel frames, panels, or complete modules — and is assembled in days rather than months.

Off-site fabrication — steel sections and panels made in the factory before reaching site.

The factory-made components vary by technique: a steel frame clad in insulated panels, precast concrete elements, panelised wall systems, or volumetric modules built as whole rooms. What unites them is the same principle — factory-controlled production first, on-site assembly second. Because fabrication and your civil foundation can run at the same time, the two timelines overlap instead of stacking, which is where prefabricated construction earns most of its time saving over conventional RCC.

Where prefabricated construction fits — and where it doesn't

Prefab construction suits buildings where speed, repeatable quality, and a predictable result matter: factories and workshops, warehouses and storage, site offices, commercial blocks, and staff facilities. Factory-made construction also holds its quality better than site work exposed to monsoon and dust, and a bolted steel structure can later be dismantled and re-erected if your operation moves.

Where prefab fits — a finished factory-built unit working on an industrial estate.

It is not the right answer for every job. The disadvantages of prefabricated construction are real and worth stating plainly: components are sized to travel by road, so very wide unbroken spans need engineering around transport limits; the design is best locked early, because late structural changes are harder once fabrication has begun; and a level foundation poured to drawing has to be ready before assembly. For a one-off building with constant design changes, conventional construction can be simpler. For a defined commercial or industrial structure you want up and working quickly, prefab is usually the stronger choice.

How SAMAN delivers prefabricated construction — and what the 3,600 sq ft unit includes

As a prefab construction service, SAMAN handles the full path: structural design, factory fabrication, transport, on-site erection by our own crew, and handover — you are not left to assemble panels yourself. The configuration shown on this page is a 120 × 30 × 20 ft building — 3,600 sq ft of floor area at a 20 ft height — on a structural steel frame clad in PUF sandwich panels, built and handed over for ₹53,45,000 to ₹53,55,000, inclusive of all taxes.

SAMAN's crew erecting the steel frame and panels of a 3,600 sq ft prefabricated building.

That scope covers the steel frame, wall and roof panels, doors and windows as configured, transport, and site assembly. You arrange a level plinth poured to the layout drawing we issue, and utility connections after structural handover. Other sizes follow the same method and are quoted per square foot. For the complete single-contract service on larger factory and warehouse projects — including IS-code structural documentation — see SAMAN's turnkey PEB construction service.

Prefabricated construction vs constructing a specific prefab building

Components delivered to site — the difference between a method page and a single fixed build.

This page explains prefabricated construction as a method and offers it as a service across building types. If your need is narrower — a particular building constructed and handed over to one specification — that is covered on our page for constructing a building to a fixed specification, where a single configuration is set out end to end. And if you expect to add bays or floors later, an expandable modular approach is designed from the outset to grow without structural rework. Tell us the use and we will point you to the right one.

Prefabricated construction: common questions

What is prefabricated construction?

It is a method where building components are manufactured in a factory and assembled on site, rather than built piece by piece in place. The result is a faster, more predictable build because factory production and site foundation work happen in parallel.

What are the disadvantages of prefabricated construction?

The main constraints are transport limits on very large components, the need to finalise the design early before fabrication starts, and a foundation that must be ready and accurate before assembly. For defined commercial and industrial buildings these are easily planned around; for constantly changing one-off designs, conventional construction can be simpler.

What is the first stage of prefabricated construction?

The first stage is structural design and a site survey. Once the layout and loads are confirmed, components are fabricated to that design while your foundation is poured in parallel — so the project starts well before anything reaches the site.

Which is better, modular or prefabricated construction?

Modular is one form of prefabricated construction — whole rooms or volumes built in the factory and craned in. "Prefabricated" is the broader term covering steel-frame, panel, and modular methods. Modular suits fast multi-room occupancy and future relocation; choose it when an expandable, relocatable layout matters more than a single fixed structure.

If you have a commercial, institutional or industrial building to put up and want it constructed as a prefabricated structure rather than built conventionally, the construction of prefabricated buildings is the service this page covers. SAMAN designs, fabricates, erects and hands over the finished building from our facilities in Bangalore and Greater Noida — you deal with one team from drawing to handover, not a chain of separate contractors. The build configured on this page is a 90 × 30 × 20 ft structure — 2,700 sq ft of floor area on a steel frame clad in PUF sandwich panels — constructed and handed over for ₹27,75,000 to ₹27,85,000, inclusive of all taxes.

A completed steel-blue prefabricated building on its plot — designed, built and handed over by SAMAN.

Which Buildings Can Be Constructed as Prefabricated Structures?

Most low- to mid-rise commercial, institutional and industrial buildings can be constructed as prefabricated structures: office blocks, showrooms and retail units, clinics and school blocks, site and administrative offices, staff facilities, and mid-size storage or light-production buildings. The structural frame and wall panels are factory-built, transported, and assembled on a prepared foundation — the same construction service applied to each building type.

Different prefabricated building types — office and light-industrial — built in sandstone-beige steel panels by SAMAN.

What changes from one building type to the next is the layout, the spans and the fit-out — not the underlying method. A single-storey office block is laid out for cabins, meeting rooms and a pantry; an institutional building such as a clinic or school block is planned around corridors and equal-sized rooms; a light-industrial or storage building is built for clear floor space and wider door openings. In every case the way we construct a prefabricated building follows the same sequence of factory fabrication and on-site assembly — only the drawing differs. If you want the underlying method explained in full before settling on a building type, our page on factory-built prefabricated construction sets out how the components are made and assembled.

What the Construction Service Covers — and Where Your Scope Begins

Across every building type the construction service covers the same defined scope. Our structural team designs the building to your floor plan and intended use, fabricates the steel frame and the wall and roof panels at our facility, transports the components to your site, and erects the building with our own crew — closing with doors, windows and the specified finishing, and a handover. You arrange two things on your side: a level plinth or foundation poured to the layout drawing we issue, and utility connections once the structure is handed over. Because that division of scope is fixed at quotation, a prefabricated building project carries no grey area over who is responsible for what.

SAMAN's crew erecting the steel frame and fixing slate-charcoal panels of a prefabricated building.

This page covers mid-scale buildings constructed as a standalone service. If your requirement is a large multi-bay factory or warehouse needing full structural documentation to IS codes and site coordination under a single contract, that is the wider turnkey PEB construction service rather than one building built to order.

The 90 × 30 ft Reference Build — Size, Materials and Price

The configuration priced on this page is a 90 × 30 × 20 ft building — 2,700 sq ft of floor area at a 20 ft eave height — constructed on a structural steel frame clad in PUF sandwich panels, and handed over for ₹27,75,000 to ₹27,85,000 inclusive of all taxes. That works out to roughly ₹1,028 per square foot for the constructed building. The figure covers the steel frame, the wall and roof panels, doors and windows as configured, transport to site, and erection by our own crew. It does not include your foundation or utility connections, which sit in your scope as set out above.

The 90 × 30 ft steel-blue reference build, complete on its plinth and handed over by SAMAN.

Other sizes follow the same construction service and are quoted per square foot, so a building larger or smaller than 2,700 sq ft is priced on the same basis rather than from a different rate card. Most buyers treat this 90 × 30 ft build as a reference point and adjust the floor area to their plot and use.

Building Across Types, or Building to One Fixed Specification?

Three nearby options serve slightly different needs, and choosing the right one saves time at quotation. This page is the right starting point when you know the building type you need constructed — an office, a commercial block, an institutional building — and want it designed and built to that use across whatever floor area suits your plot. If instead you want a single building set out end to end at one fixed configuration and price, our page on constructing a building to a set specification walks through one such build in full. And if you would rather select and purchase a building as a finished product line rather than commission a construction service, the range of prefab buildings is the better place to begin. Tell us the building type and the plot, and we will point you to the right one.

A burgundy-red prefabricated institutional building — clinic or school block — constructed by SAMAN.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to construct a prefabricated building?
The 90 × 30 × 20 ft (2,700 sq ft) steel-frame building on this page is constructed and handed over for ₹27,75,000 to ₹27,85,000 inclusive of taxes — about ₹1,028 per square foot for the finished structure. Larger or smaller buildings follow the same construction service and are quoted per square foot, with your foundation and utility connections costed separately.

Is this a construction service, or am I buying a finished building?
This is a construction service: whatever the building type — office, commercial or institutional — SAMAN designs, fabricates and erects it on your site and hands it over, rather than selling a fixed unit off a shelf. If you would prefer to choose and purchase a building from a ready product range, our prefab buildings pages are the place to start.

Can a prefabricated building be used as a permanent commercial or industrial structure?
Yes. The buildings are constructed on a structural steel frame with PUF sandwich panels — not temporary materials — so a prefabricated building serves as a permanent office, commercial or institutional structure with the working-life expectations of a conventional low-rise building, while going up in a fraction of the time.
